summary: Deployment-readiness SECURITY HARDENING regression pass — VERIFIED. All 8 previously-public bootstrap endpoints (POST /api/reset-and-seed, GET /api/populate-full/{nation}, GET /api/populate-locations/{nation}, GET /api/populate-all-nations, GET /api/initialize, GET /api/initialize/nations-images, GET /api/initialize/city-images/{nation_slug}, GET /api/initialize/location-images/{nation_slug}) now correctly return 401 for anonymous callers and 403 for authenticated non-admin callers. Handler bodies were NOT invoked with an admin token, per the safety note. Regression checks: public reads GET /api/db-status (200, counts intact), GET /api/factions (200, list) still work; standard auth flow works end-to-end (admin login -> /auth/me returns role=admin/status=active; non-admin login -> /auth/me returns role=member; anonymous /auth/me -> 401); admin-guard on non-destructive GET /api/admin/image-batch/status confirmed as 200 admin / 403 non-admin / 401 anonymous. 24/25 pytest cases PASS. The 1 failing case is unrelated to security hardening: /api/health is not defined in the backend (only /health at app-root, which is not reachable via the /api ingress). Image batch is intentionally paused per handoff note and was NOT resumed.

minor.issue: Not defined. server.py declares `@app.get("/health")` at app-root (line 72), but the external ingress only routes `/api/*` to the backend, so /api/health -> 404 and /health -> 200 HTML from the frontend. The K8s liveness probe still works (internal), but there is no public /api/health JSON endpoint. Consider adding `@api_router.get("/health")` so external callers (uptime monitors, health-check tests) can hit it.
